candidates.title: Replace and rebalance a spring-balancer-supported industrial tool
candidates.objective: On an EWA-15-class spring balancer carrying a documented 9–15 kg load, physically lock and proof-check the drum, remove the old tool, adjust spring preload with a wrench while reading the gauge, attach and support the replacement tool, release the lock, and trim preload until the tool remains balanced.
skills: controlled lock release under residual spring force
candidates.success_conditions: The drum pin must physically enter a slot and resist an upward/downward proof motion before tool removal. The replacement must be within 9–15 kg, attached before unlock, and supported during release. After adjustment, it must remain hands-off without abrupt rise or drop and traverse 70–140 mm under physical spring forces. Zero score for removing an unlocked load, releasing the balancer unloaded, snap-back, tool drop, overtravel, over-tension damage, teleportation, welding, or direct state writes. Partial milestones are verified locking, safe exchange, preload adjustment, and balanced release.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer prescribes drum locking, load verification, worm adjustment, attachment before release, and final balance checking for tool replacement; it warns that unsafe release can cause snap-back or a dropped tool.
candidates.dexterity: High. The task combines indexed locking, force-based proof checking, manipulation of a heavy suspended tool, hook handling, wrench engagement, visual gauge feedback, and guarded bimanual release.

candidates.asset_plan: A representative rigid fixture would require a six-position physical drum lock, spring-loaded pull/turn pin, worm-driven preload, readable gauge, latching hook, 1.3 m payout constraint, and 9–15 kg suspended tool. Environment tests must precede robot integration and cover all lock phases, false seating, proof loading, preload direction, hands-off balance, snap-back-relevant release, overload, overtravel, and reset repeatability. No exact-product claim is permissible.
candidates.risk: The procedure is well documented, but the acquired evidence does not dimension the lock, worm, gauge, or hook, and the full-scale 9–15 kg manipulation has not been shown feasible for the pinned YAM embodiment. The cable/spring surrogate is also unvalidated.
missing_evidence: Dimensioned EWA-15 lock-pin, drum-slot, worm, gauge, hook, and housing geometry
Manufacturer data or defensible measurements for worm ratio and spring torque versus payout
Pinned-YAM payload, grip-force, reach, and thermal validation with a 9–15 kg suspended load
Validated physical payout/spring model reproducing balance, lock holding, overtravel, and unsafe-release behavior

candidates.title: Tune an industrial robot axis shock absorber and retain the setting
candidates.objective: With an AZ-100-class axis locked out, physically manipulate the shock-absorber adjuster, cycle a representative carriage through real actuator and impact contacts, iteratively eliminate bottoming and rebound, and retain the chosen setting for repeat trials.
candidates.success_conditions: Adjustment occurs only with pneumatic and electrical energy isolated. Carriage motion, damping, rebound, and impacts must arise from modeled physical forces. Two consecutive cycles must stop without bottoming, excessive rebound, or setting drift. Zero score for powered adjustment, direct damping/state writes, disabled collision, hard-stop impact, damage, or success based only on adjuster angle.
candidates.industrial_value: The robot manual identifies shock absorbers as the cushioning mechanism for the telescoping Z and X axes and includes their deceleration performance in preventive maintenance.
candidates.dexterity: Moderate. It combines physical adjustment with closed-loop interpretation of dynamic stopping behavior, but the acquired material does not yet establish a separate lock manipulation that would raise the manual dexterity beyond adjuster rotation.

candidates.asset_plan: First obtain the shock absorber manufacturer's drawing and adjustment instructions. Then build a disclosed representative rigid carriage, impact face, external stop, adjustable damper, and physical setting-retention mechanism. Independently validate stroke, impact energy, bottoming, rebound, setting retention, sensitivity, and reset repeatability in Isaac Sim 6.1 before YAM integration.
candidates.risk: The acquired robot manual gives the application and adjustment direction but not the damper stroke, contact geometry, retention mechanism, energy envelope, or response data. Creating those now would invent essential mechanics and thresholds.
missing_evidence: Manufacturer installation and adjustment instructions for the specified shock absorber
Dimensioned body, stroke, impact face, adjuster, and setting-retention geometry
Effective-mass, velocity, energy, bottoming, and rebound limits
A defensible adjustable damping model validated in Isaac Sim
Evidence that setting retention requires a meaningful physical manipulation rather than generic knob rotation

candidates.title: Track and tension an industrial robot timing belt
candidates.objective: With robot power isolated, adjust the two-sided belt tracking/tension mechanism in small increments, manually move the axis, observe lateral belt travel, and iteratively center the belt without over-tensioning it.
candidates.success_conditions: The robot must physically operate the adjusters and manually traverse the axis after each correction. Success requires the belt to remain centered over repeated full traversals while satisfying a sourced tension or deflection criterion. Zero score for powered adjustment, direct belt-state writes, constraining the belt invisibly to the pulley center, flange climbing, excessive slack, over-tension, or component damage.
candidates.industrial_value: The manufacturer states that tracking and tensioning are both required and that incorrect adjustment can reduce performance or prematurely fail the belt.
candidates.dexterity: Potentially high because the robot must alternate between paired fine adjustments and manual full-axis motion while diagnosing the direction of belt creep. However, the essential belt behavior is deformable contact mechanics.

candidates.asset_plan: Do not implement until an already validated Isaac Sim belt/contact example is available for the pinned runtime. A faithful fixture would require dimensioned pulleys, flanges, belt profile, span, adjusters, carriage load, and a validated model of belt tension and lateral tracking. Physics tests must establish center tracking, flange climbing, slack, over-tension, manual traversal, and repeatability before robot control.
candidates.risk: This is a deformable closed-loop belt problem. No validated belt asset or solver example is present in the acquired inputs, and the manual does not provide the required pulley/belt geometry or a complete numeric tension criterion for the general AZ-100 belt.
missing_evidence: Validated belt/contact solver example compatible with Isaac Sim 6.1 and the pinned Arena/YAM revisions
Dimensioned AZ-100 belt, pulley, flange, span, adjuster, and carriage geometry
Model-specific numeric tension or deflection criterion for the selected axis
Physics validation showing that asymmetric tension produces credible lateral tracking rather than scripted motion

selection_reason: No candidate is ready, so selecting one would violate the readiness gate and would repeat the prior ambiguous-selection failure. The spring-balancer task has the strongest industrial procedure and dexterity, but it still lacks essential mechanism geometry, validated spring/payout physics, and full-scale YAM payload evidence. Shock-absorber tuning lacks essential manufacturer mechanism and dynamic-limit evidence. Timing-belt tracking requires an unavailable validated deformable implementation. Candidate selection must remain blocked until one candidate has no critical missing evidence.
